I am 68 this year, and I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and do my own sums, but what I really trust is what I have seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu and my maize about 600 kg per mu. This year I will not change much, because with 7 people in the house and some of the young ones working outside, I cannot afford a bad crop.

For the winter wheat, I will sow in October with the same improved variety I bought from the town dealer last year — about 15 kg of seed per mu. Before sowing, I will hire the rotary tiller to break up the maize stubble, 40 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I will spread one full bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time — that is 50 kg, costing about 160 yuan a bag. I know that gives me 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I will top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu — 25 kg, about 60 yuan — which adds another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. Some young people say I should cut back, but I would rather spend the extra money than risk empty grain heads. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate three times: the overwinter water before the ground freezes, the jointing water in spring, and the grain-filling water in May. Each time I run the pump it costs diesel money, but I have to do it. I will spray herbicide once after sowing and insecticide once around the flag leaf stage — two sprays total. If the weather is normal, I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will sow the hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble without plowing — there is no time to waste between harvest and sowing, and the no-till seeder service charges 30 yuan per mu. I use about 2.5 kg of hybrid seed per mu. At sowing, I will put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu — same as the wheat, 50 kg, 7.5 kg of each nutrient. Then at the big trumpet stage, I will side-dress with half a bag of urea per mu, 25 kg, adding 11.5 kg of nitrogen. The maize gets two irrigations if the summer is dry — one when the tassels come out and one during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: one herbicide and one for the corn borer. I expect 600 kg per mu if the autumn rains come on time.

All together, fertilizer alone will cost me about 2,200 yuan for the year, plus seed, diesel for the pump, sprays, and the combine harvester fees. That is a big bite out of my budget, but I have no choice. I watch what Old Wang and the others do — we all plant similar amounts, and no one is trying anything strange this year. Change is risky, and I have mouths to feed.
